essence.one_sentence: A bento menu reads as one set because its compartments share a gutter, and folding that set away lets the navigation wait out of the way until someone wants it.
essence.summary: Compartments of varied size on one gutter, warm photo cells on neutral chrome, a fold that can take the set as a whole or cell by cell, an unfold whose length is a choice, and a fade where reduced motion asks for no travel.

llm_brief.text:
On the table: a bento-inspired collapsible UI menu for a fictional specialty coffee site. From the request: a UI menu component, bento box-inspired, collapsible, for a fictional coffee company site. Researched: a specialty roaster's top bar mixes shop items with a quiz, an app and a wholesale route, and its site splits entry points between the shop, subscriptions, cafes with hours, the story and the press kit. The observed morph opens a near-black panel from a corner grid icon in about 300 ms and closes it in 117 to 133 ms. The APG disclosure example puts aria-expanded on one button per section and closes on Escape with focus returned. WCAG 2.2 asks for 24 by 24 CSS px targets or a 24 px circle of spacing around smaller ones. Specialty words in use: whole bean, single origin, blends, instant, brewing supplies.
Pool, with equal weight: compartment counts from 3 to 6 with one hero, or 9 as a 3x3 field; grid units of 4 or 12 columns; a collapsed form that is a logo bar, a row of tiles, a labelled button, an icon strip or no visible handle; motion from a quick snap to a step-by-step reveal; collapse scopes from one trigger for the whole grid to a drawer; palette roles from the stills (a dark warm ground, cream text and cells, an accent role still open).
Ways in: the first is the home angle, a grid panel that opens from a corner handle; then a row of tiles that spreads into the grid, a tin stack that lifts into a grid, a photo header that folds the rest, and folding cards with one master control. None is marked as the default.
Dials: compartment count 3 to 6; gutter 12 to 20 px; corner radius 12 to 24 px; open 80 to 400 ms; close 117 to 450 ms, read as a retract, a mirror or a settle by what it is shorter or longer than the open; icon 24 to 32 px; phone reflow to one of five forms; labels 12 to 14 px uppercase with 0.04 to 0.08 em tracking. More compartments raise the scan time for a visitor; a longer open reads as a slower unfold; a wider gutter loosens the set.
Worn paths: the usual move is a click-only div toggle; fresher: a native button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. The usual move is open-on-hover; fresher: click, Enter or Space toggles, with hover as a preview. The usual move is equal cards in a row; fresher: varied spans with one hero and shared gaps. The usual move is a stock steaming mug; fresher: a pour, a cupping spoon, a bag label or a roaster photo. The usual move is a generic nav label such as Home or Shop; fresher: a brew method, a roast and its origin, hours, a subscription, the roastery story. The usual move is web filler (seamless, elevate, curated, premium); fresher: plain specific description. The usual move reads menu as a food or drinks list; fresher: a UI menu component, a site navigation. The usual move is a bare header with a hamburger and an accordion; fresher: the grid of compartments folding from one handle or from a set of cards.
Open: platform (plain HTML, CSS and JS by default); the menu's place (site navigation, menu panel or a section, each a reading); collapse scope (whole grid, each compartment, accordion or drawer, each with its tradeoff); collapsed form (five forms, each with its tradeoff); motion (five amounts, each with its tradeoff); compartment count (five options); logo and action placement (five options); phone form (five options); palette, accent, type and the company name (see open_questions).

component.positive: A bento-inspired UI menu component for a fictional specialty coffee site. Rounded compartments of varied size on one shared gutter, on a 4 or 12 column grid. The layout can run as a hero cell with smaller cells beside and below it, as even cells, as a masonry of cards, or as one dominant cell over a strip of small ones; the count can be three to six cells, or nine as a dense field. The set collapses in one of several forms: one trigger that folds the whole grid to a bar, a trigger per compartment, an accordion with one section open at a time, or a drawer that slides from an edge. The collapsed form can be a logo bar, a row of tiles, a single labelled button, an icon strip or nothing visible, each with its findability cost. Opening can be a quick snap of 80 to 200 ms, a soft unfold of 250 to 400 ms with a small stagger, a spring with a 2 to 6 percent overshoot, or a step-by-step reveal; closing can be a retract under half the open, a mirror of the open, or a settle longer than it. The trigger is a native button with aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the region. Warm photo cells on a dark warm ground or an oat light ground carry the coffee mood, with cream or espresso text and flat neutral chrome around them. Labels are short and specific, with a 24 to 32 px icon beside each. The compartments can hold what a specialty roaster's entry points hold: a shop group, subscriptions, cafe hours, the roastery story. On a phone the layout takes one of the phone forms.
component.constraints: Targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px, or the nearest neighbour sits outside a 24 px circle. Each pair of neighbouring compartments shares one gutter value, whichever gap is chosen. Hover can preview on fine pointers and does not open the grid by itself. Focus stays on the trigger as it opens; Escape closes the grid and returns focus to the trigger. Reduced motion keeps the open and closed states and swaps travel for a fade or an instant change. Flat cells with a hairline or no border; one soft shadow on the floating panel. The company name, logo and palette are invented and labelled as invented.
component.negative: clickable div trigger, hover-only open, icon under 24 px, uneven gutters, uniform card grid, staggered masonry, accordion rows, heavy drop shadow, dark SaaS palette, steam wisps, real coffee chain logo, generic nav labels, web filler copy, motion with no reduced-motion path

params.columns: 4 or 12: the grid unit the spans divide; 12 divides into 2, 3, 4 and 6 spans
params.gap_px: 12 to 20: 12 reads tight and set-like; 20 loosens the set and separates the compartments
params.radius_px: 12 to 24: a smaller radius reads orderly; a larger one reads soft
params.cell_count: 3 to 6 with one hero, or 9 as a dense field: fewer cells scan faster; more cells hold more links
params.open_ms: 80 to 200 quick snap; 250 to 400 soft unfold (the observed open is about 300); 250 ms to 3 s for a step-by-step reveal
params.close_ms: 117 to 133 retract, about 40 percent of the open; equal to the open reads as a mirror; 300 to 450 reads as a settle
params.spring_overshoot_pct: 2 to 6 a small give at the edge; 8 to 15 a clear bounce; 20 to 40 a loose wobble where cells cross their gutters
params.stagger_ms: 0 for all at once; 20 to 40 a ripple; 30 to 70 a soft unfold; 60 to 150 a step-by-step reveal
params.handle: a 24 to 48 px square icon or logo bar, a row of tiles, a labelled button, an icon strip, or nothing visible
params.phone_form: two columns with a full-width hero; two columns without one; one column; a horizontal strip; an accordion of rows
params.reduced_motion: a fade of 0 to 100 ms, or an instant change; the state change is kept either way

component.notes: The options area and the open_questions defaults hold the choices: collapse scope, collapsed form, motion amount, compartment count, logo placement, phone form, palette, accent, type and the name. Each is one option among the others. The negative list is for any generator that takes one; a code build reads constraints.

k-req-bento.text: Do the compartments read as a bento set: varied sizes on one shared gutter, with the layout reading the build names?

test.spec: at least two cell sizes, the same gap between each pair of neighbours, and the build names the layout reading it follows (a hero with small cells, even cells, a masonry, or one dominant cell over a strip)

k-req-component.text: Does the output read as a UI menu component, a site navigation, rather than a food or drinks menu?

test.spec: the labels and placement read as site navigation links and calls to action, not as dishes or prices

k-req-collapsible.text: Does the set collapse and expand from its trigger, under the scope the build chose?

test.spec: a click on each trigger opens its part of the menu and a second click closes it; the scope the build names (whole grid, per compartment, accordion or drawer) matches what the trigger does

k-fictional.text: Are the company's name, logo and palette invented, rather than a real coffee chain's?

test.spec: the name is a placeholder, the mark is a plain wordmark, and the colours come from palette roles rather than a known brand

k-button-aria.text: Is the trigger a native button that carries aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the grid?

test.spec: a button element whose attributes include both aria-expanded and aria-controls

k-target-size.text: Does each target reach 24 by 24 CSS px, or keep its neighbours outside a 24 px circle?

test.spec: the bounding box of the trigger and each compartment link is at least 24 by 24 px at desktop and phone widths, or the nearest neighbour lies outside the 24 px circle

k-escape-focus.text: Does Escape close an open grid and return focus to the trigger that opened it?

test.spec: with the grid open, pressing Escape hides the grid and leaves focus on the trigger

k-hover-only.text: Does the trigger open on click, Enter and Space, with hover at most a preview?

test.spec: hover alone leaves the grid closed; click, Enter and Space each open it

k-reduced-motion.text: With reduced motion set, does the open and close still change state without slide, stagger or overshoot?

test.spec: with prefers-reduced-motion set to reduce, the menu still opens and closes, with no translation or scale; a fade or an instant change is the allowed alternative

k-open-timing.text: Do the open and close durations match the motion reading the build chose, and does the close fit its own reading (retract, mirror or settle)?

test.spec: record open and close durations in ms: a quick snap opens in 80 to 200, a soft unfold in 250 to 400, a step-by-step reveal in about 250 ms to 3 s; a retract closes under half the open (117 to 133 observed), a mirror closes in the open's time, a settle closes in 300 to 450; a spring reads its overshoot and settle time from bh-motion-springs

k-handle-visible.text: When the menu is collapsed, what stays on the first view, and can a first-time visitor find the menu from it?

test.spec: for the collapsed form the build uses (logo bar, row of tiles, labelled button, icon strip, or no visible handle), name what a first-time visitor sees at rest and whether it leads to the menu; a form with nothing visible is recorded with its findability cost. Reconciled with bh-opt-collapsed-form: ak-collapse-no-handle rules out only a collapsed state with no route to the menu, so the no-visible-handle form stays an option at that cost.

k-one-gutter.text: Does every gap between neighbouring compartments measure the same?

test.spec: the gap between each pair of neighbouring cells is equal and sits between 12 and 20 px

k-flat-surfaces.text: Which surfaces carry a shadow, and does the floating panel carry the one that does?

test.spec: the cells carry no shadow and the panel carries one soft shadow

k-icon-size.text: Are icons 24 px or larger, and set beside a text label?

test.spec: each icon measures 24 to 32 px and sits next to its label

k-phone-reflow.text: On a phone width, is every compartment reachable and unclipped in the phone form the build chose, with its reading order stated?

test.spec: at 390 px wide, name the phone form in use (two columns with a full-width hero, two columns without one, one column, a horizontal strip or an accordion of rows) and confirm that no compartment is clipped and its place in the reading order is kept or stated

k-labels.text: Do the compartment labels name what a customer wants, such as a brew method, a roast with its origin, hours, a subscription or the story?

test.spec: each label names something a customer does or looks for; none reads Home, About, Shop, Contact, Products or Feature one

k-filler.text: Does the copy avoid web filler words?

test.spec: \b(seamless|effortless|elevate|unlock|curated|journey|crafted with passion|premium|delight|world-class|cutting-edge|stunning)\b, expected match count zero

k-play-open.text: Does the menu open and close the way a person would try it with a pointer and then the keyboard?

test.spec: Play: click the trigger and the menu opens with the trigger reading expanded; press Escape and it closes with focus back on the trigger; open it again, press Tab into the first link, then Shift+Tab back to the trigger.

k-play-phone.text: Does the phone layout still open, reflow and keep its targets when a person plays it at phone width?

test.spec: Play at 390 px wide: tap the trigger to open the menu, then tap one compartment link; the compartments sit in the phone form the build chose, no link is clipped or overlaps its neighbour, and each tap target stays at least 24 by 24 CSS px.

k-play-reopen.text: Does a second open after a close behave like the first, with the same compartments in the same order?

test.spec: Play: open, close, open again, close again; each open shows the same compartments in the same order, and the second close returns to the collapsed handle.

collapse._about: Collapse behavior of the menu: states, triggers, motion as spreads, disclosure attributes and focus, reduced motion, targets and contrast. Observed demos (a found morph video, the APG disclosure example, a Webflow grid demo) are cited through builds_on; the values here are spreads, not settings.

options._about: options, not requirements: the collapse scope and the collapsed form are open

bh-opt-scope.text: Four collapse scopes, each with its tradeoff; the whole-grid reading is the default one.

choices.option: one trigger folds the whole grid to a bar (the default reading)
choices.tradeoff: one decision for the whole set

choices.option: each compartment folds on its own
choices.tradeoff: keeps the rest of the page in view

choices.option: an accordion keeps one open at a time
a drawer slides in from an edge

bh-opt-collapsed-form.text: Five collapsed forms, each with its tradeoff. None is the default; the consumer composes one.

choices.option: a logo bar with the trigger at its right
choices.tradeoff: carries the brand mark and the largest close target; takes a full row on a phone; needs a logo (q-name-logo)

choices.option: a row of tiles, one per compartment
choices.tradeoff: each tile can open its own compartment (the per-compartment scope); shows content while closed; more handles to reach; the row is wide on a phone

choices.option: a single labelled button, such as 'Menu' or 'Shop'
choices.tradeoff: clearest name and the easiest target to meet; the widest footprint in the corner; the label has to translate

choices.option: an icon strip, one icon per compartment or one trigger icon
choices.tradeoff: more targets in less width; each icon needs an accessible name and a 24 px target; a bean or cup can be ambiguous without a label

choices.option: no visible handle, as in the observed demos that collapse to nothing
choices.tradeoff: the cleanest page at rest and the hardest to find; ak-collapse-no-handle lists it as not wanted, kept here beside the option it rules out

bh-opt-motion.text: Five amounts of motion, each a choice. Under reduced motion each keeps its state change and loses travel, stagger and overshoot.

choices.tradeoff: fastest to use and least to watch; the change can be missed at a glance; no stagger to read

choices.option: soft unfold, 250 to 400 ms with a 30 to 70 ms stagger (the video's 300 ms open)
choices.tradeoff: shows where the menu came from; slower on repeat visits; a sequence to read on a large grid

choices.option: spring with a small overshoot, 2 to 6 percent
choices.tradeoff: the give adds character with little cost; a small rebound can read as a glitch to some viewers

choices.option: spring with a clear bounce or a large overshoot, 8 to 40 percent
choices.tradeoff: a strong rebound makes the bounce the subject; cells cross their gutters and neighbours overlap briefly; the longest wait before the menu is steady

choices.option: step-by-step reveal, from about 250 ms to about 3 s
choices.tradeoff: reads as a tour and suits a grid whose cells are the content; long sequences tire on repeat opens, and a second click can finish or reverse them

cl-closed.text: Collapsed, the menu is one small dotted grid icon in the top-right corner of an otherwise empty light page.
behaviors: While closed, the icon is the only visible part of the menu
The panel grows out of this icon's corner when it opens
signals: no panel edge or shadow visible

cl-trigger.text: A click on the icon opens the panel, and a click on the same icon closes it. Hover alone did not open it.
behaviors: The cursor reaches the icon near 3.0 s and the panel stays shut until a click near 3.55 s
A click ring sits on the icon just before the first close, near 5.95 s
The icon stays fixed as the anchor while the panel changes size
signals: cursor on icon with no change

cl-open-motion.text: Opening takes about 300 ms on an ease-out curve. The panel grows from the icon's corner while its fill darkens and its text fades in.
properties: text fades in during the morph
behaviors: The fill is still mid-grey while the box is small, and near-black once it is near full size
The ease-out fit (cubic-bezier about 0, 0, 0.58, 1) beats linear and ease-in, and an overshoot fit is not picked

cl-close-motion.text: Closing takes about 117 to 133 ms, faster than opening. The panel shrinks back into the icon's corner and the text fades out first. The panel is held open about 2.2 s before the first close.
behaviors: Easing is not settled: the fit favours an overshoot-shaped curve, but measured overshoot is 0
Only 7 and 8 frames were available, so the curve cannot be resolved more finely

tl-open.text: Open motion of about 300 ms (18 frames), a second open at 00:00:07.941 to 00:00:08.242 with the same 18 frames and ease-out fit 0.067.

tl-close.text: Close motion of about 117 ms (7 frames). A second close, 00:00:09.877 to 00:00:10.010, measures 133 ms (8 frames) with the same ambiguous easing fit (0.054).

f-closed.text: Collapsed: the dotted grid icon alone in the top-right of the blank light page.

f-mid-morph.text: Early open: a small mid-grey box at the icon's corner with faint text, not yet near-black.

f-open.text: Open: the near-black panel with three stacked links, a divider and three smaller links under it.

v-media.text: A silent 12.35 s clip of several open and close cycles on a blank light page. No captions or chapters.

apg-trigger.text: Each top-level button is a disclosure: it represents one section and toggles that section's list of links open and closed.
behaviors: Activating a button expands its dropdown; activating it again collapses it
The links for each button sit in a list nested inside that button's list item
apg-trigger.principle: The button and the list it controls form one unit, and the list nesting carries the hierarchy.

heading_path: Role, Property, State, and Tabindex Attributes

apg-states.text: The button carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, and CSS attribute selectors on aria-expanded keep the visuals in step with the state.
behaviors: Collapsed: aria-expanded is false and the container is hidden
The caret's visual state follows aria-expanded through CSS, not a separate class

apg-keys.text: Tab moves through the top-level buttons and, once a dropdown is open, into its links; Space or Enter toggles a focused button.
behaviors: Opening a dropdown adds its links to the Tab sequence right after the button
Activating a focused link also sets aria-current="page" on it

apg-close.text: An open dropdown closes on Escape, which returns focus to its button, and also when focus leaves the navigation region.
behaviors: Escape moves focus back to the button that controls the dropdown
Tabbing out of the region closes an open dropdown without a click
apg-close.principle: Closing on Escape and focus-out is tied to WCAG 2.1 1.4.13 (content on hover or focus).

apg-arrows.term: optional arrow, Home and End keys
apg-arrows.text: Arrow keys, Home and End are an optional layer on top of Tab; the example offers them as a toggle.
behaviors: Arrow support stops the page from scrolling while focus is inside the navigation
Arrows supplement Tab rather than replacing it

apg-not-menu.term: navigation, not the ARIA menu role
apg-not-menu.text: The example calls its links a menu in the colloquial sense but uses plain disclosure and links, not the menu role.
apg-not-menu.principle: Site navigation with links needs fewer keyboard interactions than a menu widget.

sc-trigger.text: The grid menu is opened by a click and closed by the same action, reversing the open sequence.
behaviors: Close plays the open sequence in reverse, so the user sees the menu return to where it came from
sc-trigger.principle: Open and close share one path, so the two states stay in step.
signals: click handler toggles open and closed

sc-open-motion.text: On open, panels scale in from bottom to top and left to right, and the text rises in a staggered motion.
behaviors: Panels arrive as a sweep, not all at once, so the grid assembles in view
Text follows the panels, so each compartment's label lands after its box
sc-open-motion.principle: Sequence the boxes first and the labels after, so a label never shows before its compartment.
signals: labels move up in a wave

sc-close-motion.text: On close the labels fade out and drop back down, and the panels scale back to zero in a staggered sequence.
behaviors: Collapsed state shows no panels, since they scale to 0; the page describes no visible bar, icon row or button
Labels leave first, then panels shrink, reversing the open order
sc-close-motion.principle: The collapsed state is what remains once every panel has scaled to zero.

bh-states.text: Collapsed, a single trigger stays visible in a corner; expanded, a dark panel of links grows out of that corner. Some demos collapse to nothing at all.
behaviors: The collapsed handle can be an icon, a logo strip or a labelled button, and each reads differently at a glance
The panel keeps the trigger as its anchor, so the trigger does not move while the size changes
With every panel at scale 0 the page shows no handle, so a first-time visitor may not find the menu
bh-states.principle: The collapsed state is the handle; what stays visible when closed decides whether anyone finds the menu.
signals: one small glyph in a corner when closed
empty page where the menu was
dark box over a light page when open

bh-triggers.text: A click or a key on the trigger toggles the panel; in the observed morph, hover alone did not open it. Escape and focus leaving the region close it.
behaviors: A second click on the same icon closes the panel, as the observed demo does
Tabbing out of the navigation closes an open panel without a click
Arrow keys, Home and End can be added as a toggle on top of Tab
bh-triggers.principle: One toggle per trigger, with Escape and focus-out as the ways out, keeps an open panel from holding focus hostage.
signals: panel still open after focus has left

bh-reduced-motion.text: With reduced motion set, open and close keep the state change and drop the slide, stagger and overshoot. The expanded state stays readable from the bar.
behaviors: An instant swap leaves the panel open or shut with no in-between frames
A short fade carries the change without any movement
The expanded state reads from aria-expanded and a visible caret, not from the motion
bh-reduced-motion.principle: The meaning of open and closed stays when the motion goes.

bh-targets-contrast.text: The trigger and each compartment link reach 24 by 24 CSS px, or keep their neighbours outside a 24 px circle; text and the trigger icon meet the contrast floors in tokens.
behaviors: A 16 px icon trigger passes only if its neighbours stay outside its 24 px circle
Compartment gaps of 12 to 20 px count toward the spacing rule
Caption text on a dark panel needs its own contrast check, separate from the grid cells
bh-targets-contrast.principle: Size and spacing decide the hit rate; contrast decides whether the labels can be read at all.

tokens.note: WCAG AA floors from general knowledge, not fetched this session

cl-open-panel.text: Expanded, the panel is a near-black rounded box at the top right, about three fifths of the page width, with three large white links, a hairline divider, and a small grey label over three smaller links.
behaviors: Primary links are larger and brighter than the secondary group
The box floats above the page with a soft shadow

bh-motion-readings.text: How a collapsible menu moves, read as two plain motions: a quick snap and a soft unfold. Springs and step-by-step reveals have their own facets.

readings.in_practice: Opens in 80 to 200 ms on ease-out; the panel is open before the eye tracks it, and the change reads as a toggle.

Opens in 250 to 400 ms; the video's 300 ms open sits here. The panel grows from the trigger corner, its fill darkens and its text fades in during the move, and a stagger of 30 to 70 ms per compartment can follow.

tokens.stagger_ms: 0 (all at once, quick snap) / 20 to 40 (ripple) / 30 to 70 (soft unfold) / 60 to 150 (step-by-step)
tokens.stagger_order: reading order / outward from the trigger, delay grows with distance / bottom to top, left to right (observed demo)

bh-motion-readings.easing: unresolved, as the source has it: the open fits ease-out best (fit 0.081 against linear 0.164, video); the close fit is ambiguous (overshoot-shaped 0.025 to 0.054, ease-out 0.169, ease-in-out 0.315) with measured overshoot 0. The soft unfold's easing is named ease-out here and ease-in-out in the vocabulary facet; both stand until a closer fit is measured.

bh-motion-springs.text: Three spring readings, from a small give to a loose wobble; each has its own overshoot and settle time.

readings.in_practice: 2 to 6 percent past full size, settling in 300 to 450 ms: a hint of give at the edge, which the spring exemplar uses.
signals: small dip past full size, then settle

readings.in_practice: 8 to 15 percent past full size, settling in 450 to 650 ms: the panel rebounds once and the cells visibly land after it. The gutters (12 to 20 px) are crossed for a frame or two, so neighbours touch.

20 to 40 percent past full size, settling in 700 ms to 1 s: a loose wobble that carries each cell past its gutter and back. The bounce is the subject of the motion. Costs: the most collisions with neighbours and the longest wait before the menu is steady.

bh-motion-reveal.text: Three step-by-step readings, set by how many compartments arrive in sequence: a short list, a medium sweep, a long tour.

readings.in_practice: 3 to 4 compartments, 80 to 150 ms apart, 250 to 500 ms in all: a deliberate list a reader can follow cell by cell.
6 to 12 compartments, 60 to 150 ms apart, 400 to 900 ms in all as the source gives it, in a sweep from bottom to top and left to right; each label rises after its box.

13 to 30 compartments, 40 to 100 ms apart with the cells overlapping, about 1 to 3 s in all. It reads as a tour; on repeat opens it tires, and a second click during the sequence can finish or reverse it.

bh-timing.term: open and close duration and easing
bh-timing.text: Measured in the found video: open 300 ms; close 117 to 133 ms (7 to 8 frames at 59.94 fps, plus or minus one frame). The three close timings sit side by side.

readings.reading: retract: close much shorter than open (observed)
readings.close_ms: 117 to 133, about 39 to 44 percent of the open
readings.in_practice: The panel snaps back into its handle; the close is over before the eye has finished following it.
The same motion runs backward at the same speed; the change reads as a reversal the eye can trace.
signals: close as long as the open
readings.held_by: no fetched source in this dump states it

readings.close_ms: about 300 to 450, 1.0 to 1.5 times the open
readings.in_practice: The panel lingers as it leaves and reads as considered; on a repeated close a slow exit can feel like lag.
signals: close as long as or longer than the open
readings.held_by: no fetched source in this dump states it

behaviors: The open is 300 ms on an ease-out curve, the measured value
A shorter close holds less motion in the eye on the way out
bh-timing.principle: Duration sets how the state change feels; the retract, the mirror and the settle are three readings of the same open and close.

bh-aria-focus.term: disclosure attributes, focus, and the menu role question
bh-aria-focus.text: Each version keeps the trigger a native button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. Whether the links take the disclosure pattern or the ARIA menu role is set out in bh-menu-role-question.
properties: hidden container out of the accessibility tree
focus stays on the trigger as the grid opens
Escape closes an open grid with focus inside the region
behaviors: Escape closes the open grid; the build can return focus to the trigger that opened it (the APG example says it closes)
A caret or chevron can follow aria-expanded through CSS, so no separate class has to stay in step
Tab order runs through the buttons and links in both views; the views differ in what the arrow keys do

bh-menu-role-question.term: links as disclosure navigation or as a menu role
bh-menu-role-question.text: Two views of what the links are, with the same visible buttons under both. The sources here describe the disclosure view for site navigation.

views.held_by: the W3C APG disclosure pattern and its navigation example, which says the example uses 'plain disclosure and links, not the menu role'
views.what_it_does: Each button toggles a list of plain links; Tab moves through them; arrow keys are an optional layer; the region is a navigation landmark.
views.cost: More Tab stops on a long grid; no arrow-key model unless one is added.

views.held_by: the ARIA menu widget, as the APG example describes it by contrast; the example's own note calls its links 'a menu in the colloquial sense' and then uses disclosure
views.what_it_does: The links become menuitems in a widget with an arrow-key model and focus managed inside it.
views.cost: Screen readers announce an application menu rather than a list of links, and the widget owns its key handling (the arrow-key model is the build's general knowledge, not fetched in this dump).

bh-menu-role-question.decides_it: What the links are: site navigation (the disclosure view) or a menu of actions (the menu-role view). The sources in this dump describe the disclosure view for site navigation; the menu-role view stays on the table for a consumer who builds the links as actions.
bh-menu-role-question.principle: Both views give keyboard and screen reader behaviour from the same visible buttons; the difference is what the links are taken to be.

bh-touch-outside.term: touch open, and a tap outside
bh-touch-outside.text: Touch has no hover, so a tap opens the panel. What a tap outside an open panel does is a choice, with three readings side by side.

readings.in_practice: A tap anywhere off the panel shuts it, as a popup does; the tap may be spent on the close rather than on the page under it.
signals: panel shut after a tap on the page
readings.cost: a tap meant for the page can be swallowed

readings.in_practice: The panel stays open until its own trigger or Escape closes it; a stray tap on the page does nothing.
readings.cost: on a phone the open panel can cover the page until the trigger is found

readings.reading: tap on the content closes, on the handle does not
readings.in_practice: A tap on the page content closes the panel; a tap on the handle or browser chrome leaves it as it is.
signals: closes on a content tap, not a handle tap
readings.cost: two rules to explain and to test

behaviors: The trigger keeps its 24 by 24 CSS px minimum (bh-targets-contrast) so a thumb can reach it

ux_principles._about: Discipline rungs for a collapsible bento menu: UI and interaction design, navigation, disclosure and accessibility, bento grid layout. Principles are named; how each plays out here is material, not orders.

ux-hick.text: Decision time grows with the number and complexity of choices.
behaviors: A closed bar with four or five labels is faster to read than an open grid of twelve links
Collapsing groups behind one trigger keeps the first decision small
ux-hick.principle: Fewer simultaneous choices, or chunked ones, speed the decision.
signals: many equal targets competing at once

ux-jakob.text: Users bring expectations from the sites they use most and expect yours to behave the same.
behaviors: A trigger labelled Menu with a standard icon is recognised without a tutorial
A grid that opens in place reads as a familiar disclosure, not a new app pattern
ux-jakob.principle: Familiar patterns cost less learning than clever ones.

ux-gestalt-proximity.text: Items placed close together read as one group; a shared bounded area also groups them. Known from general practice, not confirmed by a fetched page.
behaviors: Equal gaps between compartments make the grid read as one set
A different surface colour on a few cells splits them into a separate group
ux-gestalt-proximity.principle: Spacing and shared surfaces decide what looks related before any label is read.

a11y-disclosure.text: A disclosure is a button that shows or hides content; its aria-expanded tracks visibility.
behaviors: The trigger keeps focus when the grid opens, so keyboard users do not lose their place
Hidden compartments leave the accessibility tree when collapsed
a11y-disclosure.principle: Native buttons with aria-expanded give keyboard and screen reader behaviour for free.

a11y-target-size.text: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) asks for pointer targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or enough spacing around smaller ones.
behaviors: A 16 px icon button passes only if no other target lies inside a 24 px circle around it
Gaps between bento compartments count toward spacing
a11y-target-size.principle: Small targets are allowed when their neighbours are kept far enough away.
signals: link height under 24 px in a dense cell grid

ux-fitts.text: Time to reach a target depends on its distance and size.
behaviors: A trigger that is the largest control in the collapsed bar is the easiest one to reach
Compartments that act as links are bigger targets than their captions
ux-fitts.principle: Big, close targets are reached faster and missed less.
signals: triggers at the far edge of a bar

a11y-reduced-motion.text: WCAG advises honouring the reduce motion setting for non-essential transitions.
behaviors: Under reduced motion the grid can open with an instant state change and no slide or stagger
The expanded state stays visible in the bar even without animation
a11y-reduced-motion.principle: Motion is decoration unless it carries meaning; the meaning stays when the motion goes.

bento-overload.text: A bento grid organises content well, but packing too much into one screen can overwhelm.
behaviors: One idea per compartment lets the cell edges do the grouping
A dense collapsed bar keeps the grid from competing with the page
bento-overload.principle: The grid saves space only while each compartment stays light.
signals: cells with paragraphs and link lists

bento_grid._about: Layout facets for the bento-style compartment grid: how many compartments, which grid unit and gap, spans, reflow on a phone, and where the logo and primary action sit. Numbers are illustrative spreads unless marked sourced.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices the prompt and evidence leave open

opt-logo-action.text: Five placements for the logo and the primary action. Together they set the first read and the largest target.
behaviors: A: logo in the top-left small cell, action as the hero: logo read first, action the largest target; a small logo cell is easy to miss on a phone
B: logo in a bar outside the grid, action as the hero: brand stays clear and the grid holds only links; two regions to scan, and the bar competes with the collapsed form
C: logo as the hero, action in a small cell: brand leads; the action is a small target
D: logo and action share one wide cell across two columns: both visible with no hero; one cell carries two jobs
E: action as a full-width strip at the end of the grid: read last, after the links; easy to skip on a phone

opt-mobile-form.text: Five phone forms for the grid. Each shows a different share of the set before the first scroll.
behaviors: A: two columns, hero full width: most cells visible at once; a half-width logo cell can sit alone
B: two columns, no hero: even pairs; no full-width cell leads
C: single column stack: easiest to scan; the longest scroll, every cell at full width
D: horizontal strip: keeps the height short; cells past the right edge are easy to miss, and sideways scroll is not every visitor's first gesture
E: accordion of rows, one open at a time: each row folds its cells away, so the first view shows few links

opt-hero-count.text: Five counts, each a choice: three, four, six or nine cells with a hero, or nine or six with none. Each trades how many links the set holds against how fast it scans.
behaviors: Three cells (hero and two small): fastest to scan, fewest links; the hero carries most of the work
Four cells (hero and three small): a balance of lead and links
Six cells (two spans): more links while the set still scans as one; needs tighter copy
Nine cells (3x3 field, as in the Webflow reference): a directory of links; densest and slowest to scan; a corner nest adds a second scale
No hero, four or six even cells: calm and even, but nothing leads the eye

opt-reading-order.text: Four reading orders for the cells. Each sets the first read; a phone form can keep the order or change it.
behaviors: Row-major from the top-left: simplest to follow; the logo is read first when it sits top-left
Hero first, then clockwise: the eye lands on the lead cell before the links
Logo, then action, then links: puts the purchase path first and the links after
Tall first: a tall cell is read down before the wide cells beside it; the order breaks where the tall cell sits in a row

bg-philosophy.text: Compartments of varied size make a predictable rhythm that users can follow.
behaviors: Each compartment reads as one unit, so the set reads as one layout
bg-philosophy.principle: Visible compartments reduce the work of scanning a menu.
signals: one cell that stands apart in size

bg-bento.text: A bento-inspired menu is a set of compartments of different sizes that read together as one layout. Its large cells can be one hero, two or three, or none.
properties: no hero: near-equal cells with varied spans
behaviors: Cells of different sizes read as one set only when their gaps and edges line up
One hero leads the eye; two or three large cells share the lead
With no hero the set reads as an even mosaic, and no cell leads
When there is a large cell, it draws the eye first; the small cells hold the rest
bg-bento.principle: Varied size on a shared grid keeps the set orderly; the number of large cells decides what leads.

sc-grid-structure.text: One menu wrapper holds two grids: a 3x3 field of nine cells, and a 4x8 grid of 32 cells nested in the lower left corner. The source calls the nest smaller; with 32 cells that must mean footprint, not count.
behaviors: The nested grid sits in a corner of the larger one, so the two read as one compartment set
The nest has more cells than the field but a smaller footprint, so its cells are finer
Nine cells and a 32-cell nest give a dense field with two scales of cell
sc-grid-structure.principle: A small grid nested in a corner adds a second, finer scale without a separate container.

bg-count.text: Three to nine compartments each fit one screen, and each count sets a different scan. The cost of a high count is scan time, not a rule against it.
properties: 3 cells: a hero and two small
4 cells: a hero and three small
6 cells: two rows of three, with spans
behaviors: Each cell holds one idea, so the cell edges do the grouping at any count
Fewer cells mean fewer choices before a visitor can act; more cells hold more links
Packing too much into one screen can overwhelm (bento-overload), so a high count raises scan time
Nine cells read as a directory; three cells read as three entry points
bg-count.principle: The count sets how many choices stand between a visitor and the action.

bg-grid.text: A 4, 6 or 12 column grid with one gap value in every cell, so proximity groups the compartments into one set. The size spread runs from two sizes to a mosaic.
properties: two to six or more sizes of cell
behaviors: Two sizes read as calm and orderly; three read as a hero with support
Four or five sizes read as lively; six or more read as a mosaic that is hardest to scan
The gap counts toward the 24 px target spacing for cells that are links, so a tight gap needs cell padding
bg-grid.principle: A uniform gutter lets proximity do the grouping; the size count sets how lively the set reads.

gap_px: 20 to 24: airy, each cell stands apart

bg-reflow.text: Under a phone width the grid takes one of several forms: two columns, a single stack, or a horizontal strip. Each trades scan length against how much of the set shows at once.
behaviors: Two columns fit the most cells on one screen; a half-width logo cell can sit alone in its row
A single stack is the easiest to scan and takes the most scroll
A full-width hero is read first on a phone, so its place in the order is a choice
Paired one-column cells keep each target at least 24 by 24 CSS px
bg-reflow.principle: Reflow changes how the compartments stack; each form changes what shows before the first scroll.

coffee_voice._about: Scraped from one found coffee-roaster storefront page (ecomm.design gallery entry). Facts are the page's own; the reading for this menu is inferred.

cv-nav.text: A specialty roaster's top bar mixes shop items with a quiz, an app and a wholesale route.
behaviors: A quiz gives a shopper a second entry point beside the shop
quotes: A Huck App and a Wholesale Partners section sit in the top navigation beside the shop.
A coffee quiz is promoted from the homepage, the subscriptions page and the footer

cv-vocabulary.text: Specialty roasters name whole bean, single origin, blends, instant and brewing equipment as shop groups.
signals: filters labelled Single Origin and Blends

cv-type.text: A roaster pairs a narrow condensed display cut with a sans text face for a poster-like headline.
behaviors: A condensed headline cut gives labels a tall, compact read

hk-content.term: what a coffee site's compartments hold
hk-content.text: A specialty roaster's site splits its entry points between the shop, subscriptions, cafés, the brand story and the press kit.
behaviors: Each café gets its own page with hours, directions and an order link, listed on the homepage
A subscriptions page lists coffees on a recurring plan plus gift terms
Press and media links sit in the footer with equal weight to policies
hk-content.principle: Shoppers and wholesale buyers each get a labelled route, so the one menu serves several audiences.

exemplars._about: Exemplars as material, not copies. Each says what transfers and what does not.

ex-contra.text: A bento-style menu case study that opens from a grid icon into a dark spring-animated panel.
ex-contra.contribution: The grid glyph works as the trigger for the compartment panel.
ex-contra.never_implies: The dark SaaS palette does not transfer to a warm coffee brand.

ex-huckleberry.text: A specialty roaster with cafes, a shop and a quiz as separate entry points.
ex-huckleberry.contribution: Shows how a coffee brand separates shopping, finding a cafe and wholesale in one bar.

look_and_feel._about: Look of one compartment for a warm coffee brand: palette roles, label type, surface, imagery and icons. Moodboard values are pixel samples from photos, not brand colours; the rest are illustrative spreads. The brand is fictional: no name, logo or palette is user_stated.

options._about: options, not requirements: brand choices the prompt does not decide. The fictional company has no name, logo or palette given; none is user_stated.

opt-palette-dark.text: Option: dark roast ground near #2A1F1A with cream text near #F2E9DC.

opt-palette-oat.text: Option: oat ground near #EFE6D8 with espresso text near #3B2A22 and one dark cell per row.

opt-type-pair.text: Option: a condensed grotesque for labels with a neutral sans body, or a slab display with a serif body.

opt-name-logo.text: Option: a placeholder name and a plain wordmark, labelled as invented, so the real name can replace it.

opt-accent.text: Option: ochre, deep green or muted red as the single accent; the accent stays open until one is picked.

hk-type.text: A condensed, poster-like display cut set large against a neutral body face.
behaviors: Headings are set large enough to act as the panel's main image
Body text stays plain so the display face carries the voice
hk-type.principle: Contrast in width and weight does the hierarchy work that colour would otherwise do.

hk-color.text: Near-black type on white, with a single muted red reserved for the mark and small accents.
behaviors: Interface chrome stays neutral so product photography carries the colour
The accent appears only on the logo mark and small accents
hk-color.principle: The interface steps back when the product is the colourful thing on the page.

hk-imagery.text: Full-width panels in saturated colour, each with a short headline written as copy and a packaging or people photo.
properties: people photo in a tilted frame
behaviors: Each panel carries one headline and one image, so a small compartment reads at a glance
Packaging is shown upright and large rather than as a small thumbnail
hk-imagery.principle: A single saturated field and one image make a compartment legible at phone width.

lf-palette-roles.term: palette roles for a warm coffee menu
lf-palette-roles.text: Roles, not a fixed palette: a dark warm ground, a cream text and cell role, and an accent role left open.
behaviors: Dark warm ground carries photo cells; cream carries text cells
Chrome stays neutral so the photos carry the warmth
lf-palette-roles.principle: Photos set the warmth; the chrome steps back.

tokens.share_reading_a: dark ground 40 to 55 percent, cream 30 to 40, accent 5 to 10
tokens.share_reading_b: cream ground 65 to 75 percent, dark ink 15 to 20, accent 5 to 10

lf-type.text: A condensed display cut in uppercase for labels, a neutral sans for body and detail lines.
behaviors: A tall condensed label reads at a glance in a small cell
Body text stays plain so the label carries the voice
lf-type.principle: Width and weight contrast does the hierarchy work.

lf-imagery-icons.term: imagery and icons in small compartments
lf-imagery-icons.text: One subject per small cell, cropped tight, with the label beside the icon rather than the icon alone.
behaviors: A tight crop fills a small cell without a caption
An icon at 24 px or more keeps the target size
lf-imagery-icons.principle: One subject and one headline make a small compartment legible at phone width.

lf-surface.text: Flat rounded compartments with a hairline or no border; depth only on the floating panel.
properties: one soft shadow on the panel
behaviors: The floating panel is the only element with a shadow
Neighbouring cells are separated by the gutter, not by borders
lf-surface.principle: Depth marks what moves; everything else stays flat.

tokens.shadow: none on cells; one soft shadow on the panel

lf-palette-samples.term: warm tones sampled from coffee stills
lf-palette-samples.text: Dark warm browns and one pale pink-cream, sampled from the coffee stills; photo-cell tones, not a palette.

lf-accent-unknown.text: The accent is unresolved: the sources disagree. Scrape 28 reads one muted red; the Huckleberry screenshot's pixel sample reads teal #6DC0B2. Neither is stated as the accent.
lf-accent-unknown.principle: Two sources disagree, so the accent stays unknown rather than being chosen.

moodboard._about: Moodboard of images that bear on the bento coffee menu: found online, researched; palettes are photo samples, not print specs.

mb-coffee-stills.term: coffee stock stills: dark wood and warm side light

Bento examples work through gutters, not colour
mb-shared.principle: Photo imagery sets the warmth; the grid sets the order.
mb-shared.text: Coffee imagery is dark and warm, the bento examples are light and orderly, and the screenshot is light with one accent. Transfers: dark-warm palette role for photo cells, light surface for text cells, one tight subject per small cell.

vocabulary._about: Quality readings for the two prompt qualities, plus keyword registers and search phrases. Readings are side by side; none is the default.

q-bento.text: How tight or loose the compartment grid reads.

readings.in_practice: Even 12 to 16 px gutters, two cell sizes at most, one shared corner radius, and one hero cell in the top row; the grid reads as one rule repeated.
Cells span one to three columns and come in four or more sizes, with mixed radii and a staggered rhythm; it looks like a collage of compartments packed in a hurry.
One dominant cell carries a large image or headline; small cells hold short captions and icons; whitespace does the grouping and surfaces stay flat.
Soft shadows, slightly uneven radii and warm paper-toned surfaces; the compartments look like lidded tins on a pantry shelf.

kw-technical.text: Words for the grid and the disclosure, as a builder or a designer would type them.

kw-mood.text: Words for how a bento menu looks and feels.

sq-menu-patterns.text: Phrases a builder would type to find examples of this menu.

q-collapsible.text: How the grid folds and unfolds in time.

readings.in_practice: The grid opens or closes in under 200 ms on an ease-out curve with no stagger; a click that happens to reveal content.
250 to 400 ms on an ease-in-out curve; each compartment rises and fades 20 to 40 ms after the one before, so the grid opens outward from the trigger.
A spring near critical damping lets the panel overshoot a few pixels and settle; compartments land with a slight bounce.
Compartments appear one at a time in reading order with a visible pause between each, like a telescoping sequence the eye follows; it runs long, so it suits short menus only.

associations._about: Brings adjacent to bento and collapsible: lineages, practices and objects a model would not say first. Seed material only.

assoc-bento-lineage.text: Compartment systems from lunch boxes to modular bins, each with its own idea of order.
contribution: Jubako: stacked lacquer boxes, one tier per course; the grid as a stack
Masala dabba: a round steel spice tin with small lidded cups; equal small compartments
Gridfinity: a base-unit grid for workshop drawers; cells that snap together
Mondrian grid paintings: rectangles of unequal size held by black lines
Egg-crate and seed-tray cells: equal cells, the plainest bento

assoc-collapsible.text: Things that fold, pleat or nest; each suggests a different motion.
contribution: Sensu fan: pleats that open in one sweep and close flat
Accordion bellows: one pleat per section
Tambour roll-top slats: a flexible shutter that slides into a housing
Telescoping antenna: sections that nest and extend in order

assoc-coffee.text: Coffee settings and objects that share the grid or the fold.
contribution: Kyoto kissaten: siphon and drip houses, wood and dim light, a menu on a wall board
Nordic light roast: clear, bright cups on pale, clean surfaces
Pour-over ritual: a timed sequence of bloom and drawdown
Cupping table: a row of small cups in a grid, the first tasting layout
Collapsible silicone dripper or travel cup: a folding object people already know

exclusions._about: Worn paths: where a bare prompt's likely build falls short of the user's words. Scopes and options, not orders.

ex-bare-default.text: A plain header with a logo, text links and a hamburger; the menu opens as a stacked list with an accordion, equal cards and stock coffee photos.
behaviors: The collapse hides the whole menu behind one toggle, with no keyboard or reduced-motion path
Once the cells are equal and listed, the bento is gone
ex-bare-default.principle: A bare prompt gets a menu; the request asked for compartments that read as one set.
